column4: the x86-64 ALU opcode group the encoder emits, fixed by the instruction set; another instruction is a new variant with its encoding, not a library extension
the sixteen x86-64 condition codes, fixed by the instruction set; there is nothing for library code to extend
the x86-64 shift group the encoder emits, fixed by the instruction set; another shift is a new variant with its encoding, not a library extension

the exact field set of an accepted generation's audit record in the `jet.budget-manifest` schema; another field is a new manifest schema version that the store writes and reads together, not a library extension

the budget report measurement fields a prior baseline generation must share with the candidate to be compared with it; another field changes which stored reports compare, so it lands with a budget report schema version
the budget report subject fields (target triple, target class, profile) a prior baseline generation must share with the candidate; another field lands with a budget report schema version

the three ways `jet budget update` accepts a report, each written as the audit `kind` (`pass`, `bootstrap`, `exception`) the manifest reader checks; another way is a new audit kind in the manifest schema

the three states the baseline staleness rule gives a budget's newest compatible generation (none, fresh, stale), which decide whether a bootstrap may replace it; another state is a change to that rule, not a library extension
the artifact file kinds Jet writes, each paired with its fixed extension in ARTIFACT_KINDS; another kind is a new artifact format with its own extension and reader, not a library extension
the argument shapes an interpolation format selector takes in its parentheses; another shape is a change to the interpolation grammar through the syntax registry
the token classes the highlight generator assigns every grammar token for the editor grammars it writes; another class is a change to the generated grammars, not a library extension
the binary operators the grammar parses; a new operator is a language change through the syntax registry, and library code names an operation as a function instead
the IR instruction set every backend lowers; library code reaches new behavior through Core calls and runtime routes, and a new op lands with its lowering in every backend
the checkout trees (AGENTS.md repository layout) whose #Tests the coverage row requires some suite to run; another tree is a repository layout change that lands with this row, not a library extension
the checkout trees (AGENTS.md repository layout) whose packages the packages suite runs; another tree is a repository layout change that lands with this row, not a library extension
